Counsel,

Thank you for circulating Seller’s initial draft. Buyer has reviewed and proposes the following principal comments for incorporation into the next draft:

1. Purchase Price. Buyer cannot accept USD 45,000,000 on the current diligence record. Buyer proposes USD 38,000,000, subject to satisfactory completion of diligence and confirmation of the financial statements.

2. Closing. Closing should occur on the later of 45 days after signing and satisfaction or waiver of customary closing conditions, including completion of confirmatory diligence, receipt of required consents/approvals, bring-down of representations, and no material adverse change.

3. Representations. The financial statement representation should be expanded to state that the financial statements: (a) were prepared in accordance with GAAP consistently applied; (b) fairly present the financial condition and results of operations of the Company; (c) are complete and accurate in all material respects; and (d) do not omit liabilities required to be reflected or disclosed. Seller should also represent absence of undisclosed liabilities and absence of any material adverse change since the statement date.

4. Remedies/Indemnity. The draft should include customary survival and indemnification provisions for breaches of representations, warranties, and covenants, supported by a 10% purchase price escrow or holdback for at least 18 months, with customary basket and cap mechanics to be discussed.

5. Confidentiality. The confidentiality covenant should be mutual and include customary exceptions for disclosures to representatives, financing sources, auditors, tax/legal advisors, and disclosures required by law, regulation, legal process, or stock exchange rules.

Please revise the draft accordingly, or let us know if Seller would prefer that Buyer circulate a markup.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. At Closing, the Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 42,500,000 for the Shares, by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Seller in writing.

2. Closing; Closing Conditions. Closing shall occur on the later of (a) 30 days after signing and (b) the date that is three Business Days after satisfaction or waiver of the conditions set forth in this Section 2, or on such other date as the parties may agree in writing. The parties’ obligations to close shall be subject to: (i) the bring-down of the representations and warranties as of Closing, except where the failure to be true and correct would not reasonably be expected to be material; (ii) performance in all material respects of pre-Closing covenants; (iii) receipt of required third-party and governmental consents or approvals identified by the parties prior to signing; (iv) completion of confirmatory diligence limited to matters reasonably requested by Buyer prior to signing and not inconsistent with the diligence materials made available by Seller; and (v) no Material Adverse Effect having occurred after signing. For purposes of this Agreement, “Material Adverse Effect” means any event, change, or circumstance that has had, or would reasonably be expected to have, a material adverse effect on the business, assets, liabilities, financial condition, or results of operations of the Company, taken as a whole, excluding effects arising from general economic, market, industry, legal, regulatory, political, or force majeure conditions except to the extent disproportionately affecting the Company.

3. Representations. Seller represents that the financial statements delivered to Buyer were prepared in accordance with GAAP consistently applied, fairly present in all material respects the financial condition and results of operations of the Company as of the dates and for the periods indicated, are complete and accurate in all material respects, and do not omit liabilities required by GAAP to be reflected or disclosed therein, except as would not be material to the Company taken as a whole. Except as reflected in the financial statements, incurred in the ordinary course of business since the date thereof, or disclosed to Buyer, Seller has no knowledge of any undisclosed liability of the Company that would be material to the Company taken as a whole. Since the date of the most recent financial statements delivered to Buyer, there has not occurred any Material Adverse Effect.

4. Confidentiality. Each party shall keep confidential the terms of this Agreement and all non-public information received from the other party in connection with the transactions contemplated hereby, and shall use such information solely for purposes of evaluating, negotiating, financing, consummating, and administering such transactions. A party may disclose such information to its representatives, affiliates, financing sources, auditors, tax advisors, legal counsel, and other professional advisors who have a need to know and are informed of the confidential nature of the information, and as required by applicable law, regulation, legal process, governmental authority, or stock exchange rule; provided that, to the extent legally permissible and reasonably practicable, the disclosing party shall give prior notice to the other party and cooperate in seeking confidential treatment. These obligations shall not apply to information that is or becomes public other than through breach of this Agreement, was already known to the receiving party without restriction, is independently developed without use of confidential information, or is received from a third party not known to be subject to a confidentiality obligation.

5. Indemnification; Survival; Escrow. The representations and warranties in this Agreement shall survive Closing for 12 months, except for fundamental representations, which shall survive for the applicable statute of limitations. From the Purchase Price, 5% shall be deposited at Closing into an escrow account with a mutually acceptable escrow agent for 12 months to secure Seller’s indemnification obligations for breaches of representations, warranties, and pre-Closing covenants. Seller shall indemnify Buyer for losses finally determined or mutually agreed to arise from such breaches, subject to a deductible basket equal to 1% of the Purchase Price, after which only amounts in excess of the basket shall be recoverable. Seller’s aggregate liability for non-fundamental representation and warranty claims shall not exceed the escrow amount, and Seller’s aggregate liability for all claims other than fraud or intentional misconduct shall not exceed the Purchase Price. Buyer shall indemnify Seller for breaches of Buyer’s representations, warranties, and covenants. The parties shall include customary procedures for notice, defense, mitigation, and third-party claims in the definitive agreement.

receiver.requested_changes:
Buyer appreciates Seller’s movement and can proceed toward signing subject to the following revisions:

1. Purchase Price: revise to USD 40,750,000. Buyer’s confirmatory diligence and review of the protection package do not support USD 42,500,000, particularly given the proposed limitations on post-closing recourse.

2. Closing Conditions / Confirmatory Diligence: retain Seller’s framework, but revise clause 2(iv) to permit Buyer to complete confirmatory diligence on financial, tax, legal, customer, supplier, employment, and compliance matters reasonably requested before signing or reasonably arising from materials provided before Closing. Confirmatory diligence should be satisfied only if Buyer has not identified any matter that would reasonably be expected to be material to the Company or the transaction.

3. Financial Statements / Undisclosed Liabilities: remove the knowledge qualifier from the undisclosed-liabilities representation. Seller is in the best position to stand behind liabilities of the Company. The representation should cover all liabilities required to be reflected or disclosed under GAAP and all other material liabilities, except those disclosed in a schedule accepted by Buyer.

4. Bring-Down: Seller representations should be brought down at Closing as true and correct in all respects, except that representations already qualified by materiality or MAE are brought down in all respects and other representations may be subject to a materiality standard.

5. Indemnification / Escrow:
   a. Escrow to be 10% of the Purchase Price for 15 months.
   b. General survival period to be 18 months.
   c. Basket to be a tipping basket of 0.5% of the Purchase Price, after which all losses from dollar one are recoverable.
   d. Cap for non-fundamental representation claims to be 15% of the Purchase Price, not limited solely to the escrow.
   e. Fundamental representations, tax matters, capitalization/title to shares, authority, broker fees, fraud, intentional misconduct, and equitable remedies should be carved out from the general cap as customary.
   f. Losses should include reasonable attorneys’ fees and costs of investigation/enforcement.

6. Materiality Scrape: for indemnification purposes, materiality, Material Adverse Effect, and similar qualifiers should be disregarded for determining losses and whether a breach occurred, except in the no-MAE representation and where the qualifier defines the scope of a listed schedule item.

7. Third-Party Claim Procedures: add customary provisions requiring prompt notice, Buyer control of claims affecting the business or seeking non-monetary relief, no settlement without Buyer consent where settlement imposes non-monetary obligations or does not include a full release, and Seller cooperation at Seller’s expense for indemnifiable claims.

8. Confidentiality: acceptable in principle, subject to ensuring Buyer may disclose information to debt/equity financing sources and potential syndicate participants and their representatives under customary confidentiality obligations.
receiver.message_back:
Counsel,

Thank you for the revised draft. Buyer appreciates Seller’s movement and the inclusion of more developed closing, diligence, representation, confidentiality, and indemnity mechanics. We are close on structure, but Buyer cannot accept the current economics and recourse package as drafted.

Buyer is prepared to move forward on the basis of a purchase price of USD 40,750,000, paired with the revisions set out below. The current USD 42,500,000 price, together with a 5% escrow, 12-month survival period, knowledge-qualified undisclosed-liabilities representation, deductible basket, and escrow-only recovery for non-fundamental claims, does not provide Buyer with sufficient protection for the risk profile of the transaction.

Please revise as follows:

1. Purchase price to be USD 40,750,000.
2. Confirmatory diligence to cover financial, tax, legal, customer, supplier, employment, and compliance matters reasonably requested before signing or reasonably arising from materials provided before Closing, and to be satisfied only if Buyer has not identified a matter reasonably expected to be material to the Company or the transaction.
3. Remove the knowledge qualifier from the undisclosed-liabilities representation.
4. Bring-down condition to require materiality-qualified representations to be true in all respects and other representations to be true except where failure would not be material.
5. Escrow to be 10% for 15 months; general survival to be 18 months.
6. Basket to be a 0.5% tipping basket, with recovery from dollar one once exceeded.
7. Cap for non-fundamental representation claims to be 15% of the purchase price and not limited solely to the escrow.
8. Fundamental representations, tax matters, capitalization/title, authority, broker fees, fraud, intentional misconduct, and equitable remedies to be carved out from the general limitations.
9. Add a customary materiality scrape for indemnification purposes.
10. Add customary third-party claim procedures and confirm that losses include reasonable attorneys’ fees and enforcement/investigation costs.
11. Confidentiality is acceptable in principle, provided Buyer may disclose to financing sources and potential syndicate participants and their representatives under customary confidentiality obligations.

If Seller can accept these points, Buyer is prepared to turn a clean draft promptly and work toward signing on the agreed timetable.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP
